'''"Come out ye' black and whites"''' is a [[Perastan]] song a about the [[Pesteran-Astorian War]], composed by Dean O'Malley and written by Finn Fitzgerald in 1943 it extols the achievements of [[Perastan Republican Army]] and is an insult to [[Legion of Astoria|Astoria]].

= Significance =
'''"Come out ye' black and whites"''' was composed originally by frontline soldiers as a rallying song and became a popular song and is revered among [[Anti-Astorianists]]. it became so popular that the national anthem was changed to the song.

= Lyrics =
I was born in a Bantry street,

where the Loyal drums do beat,

the loving Astorian boots, tried to walk all over us,

and every single night,

when me commander would come home tight,

he'd invite the soldiers out with this chorus:


Come out ye' black and whites!

Come out and fight me like a man!

Show your wife how you won medals down in Bakoria!

Tell her how the PRA,

made you run like hell away,

from the green and lovely fields of Suzmenia!


Come tell us how you slew,

Like the peasants they had muskets and bows and arrows!

How bravely you faced one,

And you frightened them damn natives to the marrow!
